sections.text:
1 De Abumasare, supra, p. 91, n. 4. Verbis allatis incipit eius Liber florum editus
Venetiis a. 1495, ab ignoto scriptore translatus; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 361 d.
2 Codices Abumasaris Libri experimentorum enumeravit Steinschneider, Sera-
peum, 1870, p. 309; cf. Zum specul., p. 361 e.
3 De Masch'Allah, supra, p. 87, n. 3. Eius Liber de revolutione annorum mundi,
editus est Venetiis a. 1493; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 379 d. ; Suter, op. cit., p. 6, § 9.
4 Albertus primam partem Operis quadripartiti de Iudiciis astrorum designat
quod Ioannes Hispalensis a. 1142 composuit et editum est Norimbergae a. 1548,
cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 374 e; cf. infra, p. 95, n. 5.
5 Ja'qûb ben Ishâq el Kindî, illustrissimus Arabum philosophus, mortuus Bag-
dadae circa a. 873 p. C. Libro laudato titulus est De imbribus sive de temporum
mutatione et incipit verbis : Rogatus fui quod manifestarem, in editione Parisina
a. 1540, quam inspexi, ubi simul cum Iaphar De mutatione temporis prodiit. —
Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 362, n. 10; Suter, op. cit., p. 23, § 45. — Vide etiam
cod. Paris. 7440, ubi exstat f. 8 opusculum Alkindi de aeribus et pluviis.
6 De hoc libro, cf. n. 5. — Auctorem eius Abumasarem (Dja'far ben Muhamed
el Balchî, p. 91, n. 4) esse innuit Albertus; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 369, n. 20.
7 Liber de mutatione temporum Indorum, editus est a Libri, Hist. des sciences
mathém., I, 372. Est retractatio libri Gaphar (supra, n. 6) ; cf. Steinschneider, l. c.,
p. 394, n° 49.
7 Cf. supra, p, 91, n. 3.
sections.en:
1 On Albumasar, above, p. 91, n. 4. With the words cited begins his Book of Flowers published
at Venice in 1495, translated by an unknown writer; cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 361 d.
2 The codices of Albumasar's Book of Experiments were enumerated by Steinschneider, Sera-
peum, 1870, p. 309; cf. Zum specul., p. 361 e.
3 On Masch'Allah, above, p. 87, n. 3. His Book on the revolution of the years of the world,
was published at Venice in 1493; cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 379 d. ; Suter, op. cit., p. 6, § 9.
4 Albert designates the first part of the Quadripartite Work on the Judgments of the Stars
which John of Seville composed in 1142 and was published at Nuremberg in 1548,
cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 374 e; cf. below, p. 95, n. 5.
5 Ja'qûb ben Ishâq el Kindî, the most illustrious philosopher of the Arabs, died at Bag-
dad around 873 A.D. The title of the praised book is On showers or on the change of weather
and begins with the words: I was asked to make manifest, in the Parisian edition
of 1540, which I inspected, where it appeared together with Iaphar On the change of weather. —
Cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 362, n. 10; Suter, op. cit., p. 23, § 45. — See also
cod. Paris. 7440, where there exists on f. 8 the opuscule of Alkindi on airs and rains.
6 On this book, cf. n. 5. — Albert hints that its author is Albumasar (Dja'far ben Muhamed
el Balchî, p. 91, n. 4); cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 369, n. 20.
7 The Book on the change of weather of the Indians, was published by Libri, Hist. des sciences
mathém., I, 372. It is a retractation of the book of Gaphar (above, n. 6) ; cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit.,
p. 394, n° 49.
7 Cf. above, p, 91, n. 3.

summary.headline: Astrological Works on Weather
summary.text: A catalogue passage on astrological works concerning comets, weather changes, planetary accidents, and winds, citing Albumasar’s Book of Flowers and Book of Experiments, Messahallah’s Book of Revolutions, John of Seville’s First Part, Alkindi’s work on rains and weather, Gaphar or Geazar’s book, the Indian Book of the Times, and Ptolemy’s Quadripartite Book.
